The Lag-Llama framework constructs a probabilistic time-series forecasting system by combining lagged observations and datetime features into a structured input vector. This vector is processed by a causal decoder-only transformer, which generates latent representations capturing temporal dynamics. The final output head maps these latents to Student-t distribution parameters, allowing for uncertainty-aware predictions. The model is trained using negative log-likelihood of the Student-t distribution, optimizing for CRPS and other probabilistic metrics. In GSI, this enables Bayesian inference over uncertain outcomes, while in GSE, it supports dynamic state transitions based on historical and calendar-driven inputs. Failure modes include inadequate lag specification, poor datetime encoding, or insufficient model capacity for complex temporal structures.
